Inertia: Inertia is the tendency of an object to keep doing what it is already doing. A body at rest stays at rest, and a moving body keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed, unless a net force acts on it. That is Newton first law. When a bus brakes hard, passengers lurch forward because their bodies still have the forward motion.
Friction: Friction is a force that opposes the relative motion of two surfaces in contact. Walking needs friction between shoes and the ground. On a wet floor friction drops, so people slip. Rough surfaces usually give more friction than smooth ones.
Gravity: Gravity is the force that pulls objects toward each other. On Earth it pulls everything toward the centre of the planet, so objects fall down. Weight is the gravitational force on a mass. Mass stays the same everywhere; weight can change if gravity changes.
Osmosis: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules through a partially permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration. Plant roots take in water by osmosis. Putting salt on a slug draws water out and harms it.
Diffusion: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration. Perfume spreads across a room by diffusion. Oxygen moves from the air in the lungs into the blood by diffusion.
Photosynthesis: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make food using sunlight, carbon dioxide and water. Chlorophyll in leaves traps light energy. The products are glucose and oxygen. Without photosynthesis there would be little free oxygen in the air.
Respiration: Respiration is the process by which living cells release energy from food. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water. The energy is stored as ATP. It is not the same as breathing, which only moves air in and out of the lungs.
Ohm's law: Ohm law states that the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it, if temperature stays constant. Written as V equals I times R. A larger resistance means a smaller current for the same voltage.
Series circuit: In a series circuit components are connected one after another in a single path. The same current flows through every component. Total resistance is the sum of individual resistances. If one bulb blows in a simple series string, the whole path opens.
Parallel circuit: In a parallel circuit components sit on separate branches. Voltage across each branch is the same. Currents in the branches add to the total current. Home lighting uses parallel wiring so one failed bulb does not switch off the whole house.
Reflection: Reflection is when light bounces off a surface. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Smooth mirrors give clear images. Rough walls scatter light, so you do not see a sharp image of yourself on a wall.
Refraction: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium into another, for example air into water. A stick looks bent in water because light changes speed and direction at the surface. Lenses use refraction to focus light.
Kinetic energy: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because it is moving. It increases with mass and with the square of speed. A fast car has far more kinetic energy than a slow one of the same mass, which is why high-speed crashes are more destructive.
Potential energy: Potential energy is stored energy due to position or state. A book on a high shelf has gravitational potential energy. A stretched rubber band has elastic potential energy. When the book falls, potential energy converts into kinetic energy.
Acid: An acid is a substance that produces hydrogen ions in water and has a pH less than 7. Acids taste sour and turn blue litmus red. Hydrochloric acid in the stomach helps digest food. Strong acids can burn skin and must be handled carefully.
Base: A base is a substance that can neutralize an acid. Many bases produce hydroxide ions in water and have a pH greater than 7. Soap is mildly basic. Alkalis are bases that dissolve in water. Bases turn red litmus blue.
Neutralization: Neutralization is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water. Indigestion tablets neutralize excess stomach acid. Farmers may add lime to acidic soil to raise pH toward neutral.
Mitosis: Mitosis is cell division that produces two daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes as the parent. It is used for growth and repair in the body. Skin cells divide by mitosis to replace damaged tissue.
Meiosis: Meiosis is cell division that produces gametes with half the chromosome number of the parent. In humans that means 23 chromosomes in sperm or egg. When fertilization occurs the full number is restored.
Force: A force is a push or a pull. Forces can change the speed, direction or shape of an object. Force is measured in newtons. Weight is the force of gravity on a mass.
Pressure: Pressure is force divided by area. A sharp knife cuts easily because the force acts on a small area, so pressure is high. Lying on soft sand spreads weight over a larger area and reduces pressure.
Density: Density is mass per unit volume. Lead is denser than wood, so a small lead piece can weigh more than a larger wood block. Objects denser than water usually sink; less dense objects float.
Voltage: Voltage, or potential difference, is the energy transferred per unit charge between two points in a circuit. It is measured in volts. A higher voltage can drive a larger current through the same resistance.
Electric current: Electric current is the flow of electric charge. In metal wires the moving charges are electrons. Current is measured in amperes. Conventional current is drawn from positive to negative even though electrons drift the other way.
Conduction: Thermal conduction is the transfer of heat through a material without the material itself moving as a whole. Metals are good conductors because free electrons carry energy quickly. Wood and plastic are poor conductors, so they make good handles for cooking pots.
Convection: Convection is heat transfer by the movement of a fluid. Warm air rises and cooler air sinks, forming a convection current. Home radiators heat a room mainly by convection of air.
Radiation heat: Thermal radiation is heat transfer by electromagnetic waves. It does not need a medium. The Sun warms Earth by radiation through space. Dark surfaces absorb radiation better than shiny ones.
Enzyme: Enzymes are biological catalysts made of protein. They speed up chemical reactions in living cells without being used up. Amylase in saliva starts breaking starch into sugar. High temperature can denature enzymes and stop them working.
Atom: An atom is the smallest unit of an element that still has the properties of that element. It has a nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons in shells around it. Different elements have different numbers of protons.
Molecule: A molecule is two or more atoms chemically bonded together. Oxygen gas is O2, two oxygen atoms. Water is H2O. Molecules of a compound have fixed ratios of atoms.
Evaporation: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into a gas at the surface, below the boiling point. Faster molecules escape into the air. Sweat cools the body because evaporation takes heat from the skin.
Condensation: Condensation is the change of a gas into a liquid when it cools. Water drops form on a cold drink bottle as water vapour in the air condenses. Clouds form when water vapour high in the sky cools and condenses.
Boiling: Boiling is rapid vaporization of a liquid throughout its bulk at a fixed temperature called the boiling point. For pure water at standard pressure that is 100 degrees Celsius. Bubbles of vapour form inside the liquid, not only at the surface.
Melting: Melting is the change of a solid into a liquid at the melting point. Ice melts at 0 degrees Celsius under standard pressure. Heat energy breaks the rigid structure so particles can slide past each other.
Speed: Speed is distance travelled per unit time. It is a scalar, so it has magnitude only, no direction. Average speed equals total distance divided by total time. SI unit is metres per second.
Velocity: Velocity is speed in a stated direction. It is a vector. Changing direction changes velocity even if speed stays the same. A car turning a corner at constant speed still has changing velocity.
Acceleration: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. Speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction all count as acceleration. SI unit is metres per second squared.
Momentum: Momentum is mass times velocity. It is a vector. In a closed system total momentum stays constant if no external force acts. That is conservation of momentum, used in collision problems.
Work: Work is done when a force moves an object in the direction of the force. Work equals force times distance moved in the force direction. SI unit is the joule.
Power: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy. Power equals work divided by time. SI unit is the watt. A more powerful motor can lift the same load in less time.
Lens: A lens is a shaped piece of transparent material that refracts light to form an image. Convex lenses converge light and can magnify. Concave lenses diverge light. Eyes and cameras use lenses.
Sound: Sound is a longitudinal wave produced by vibrating objects. It needs a medium such as air. Higher frequency means higher pitch. Louder sounds have larger amplitude.
Light: Light is electromagnetic radiation that the human eye can detect. It travels in straight lines in a uniform medium at about 300 thousand kilometres per second in vacuum. It can be reflected, refracted, and absorbed.
Magnetism: Magnetism is a force caused by moving electric charges and the spin of electrons. A magnet has a north and south pole. Like poles repel; unlike poles attract. Earth has a magnetic field that compasses use.
pH scale: The pH scale measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is from 0 to 14. pH 7 is neutral. Below 7 is acidic; above 7 is alkaline. Universal indicator shows pH by colour change.
Rusting: Rusting is the corrosion of iron in the presence of air and water. The reddish-brown product is hydrated iron oxide. Painting, oiling, or galvanizing iron slows rusting by keeping oxygen and water away.
Catalyst: A catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up. It lowers the activation energy. Enzymes are biological catalysts. Platinum is used as a catalyst in some industrial processes.
Food chain: A food chain shows how energy passes from one organism to another. It starts with a producer such as a green plant. Then come primary consumers, secondary consumers, and so on. Arrows point to the eater.
Ecosystem: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms interacting with each other and with non-living factors like soil, water, and climate in a given area. A pond, a forest, and a coral reef are ecosystems.
DNA: DNA is the molecule that carries genetic information in cells. It has a double helix structure of paired bases. Genes are sections of DNA that code for proteins. DNA is copied before cell division.
Cell: The cell is the basic unit of life. Animal cells have a membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus. Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts, and often a large vacuole. Unicellular organisms are made of one cell.
